figures.message: A logistic regression's out-of-fold disagreements are mostly the flipped labels, so dropping them and refitting keeps accuracy near the clean level while plain logistic regression and an untuned MLP fall with noise.
figures.layout: Three flat pastel rounded panels left to right joined by thick rounded arrows, each with a numbered circle and a plain sans-serif title. (1) 'Noisy labels': a 4x6 grid of small digit thumbnails with class tags; about a quarter of the tags are flipped and outlined in muted red. (2) 'Drop disagreements': five fold blocks; one fold is predicted by a purple (#4E2A84) network-card icon fit on the other four; samples whose prediction differs from the tag get a small cross. Under it, one horizontal stacked bar of all dropped samples pooled over the noisy runs, split into 'flipped' (purple, about 71%) and 'clean' (lavender #F1EEF7 with purple outline), labeled with the pooled precision. (3) 'Refit': grouped bars, two small groups (Digits, Breast cancer), x = noise 0/20/40%, three bars each: Logistic regression (muted blue), MLP (muted orange), Filter (ours, accent purple #4E2A84); error bars are sd over 5 seeds, seed dots overlaid, y = test accuracy (%) from 50 to 100, legend above the panel. Panel 3 carries the result, so the figure shows the problem (flips, accuracy drop) and the result together.
figures.caption_draft: Out-of-fold disagreement finds flipped labels, and refitting without them keeps a linear model accurate under label noise. (1) A training set with symmetric label flips. (2) Each sample is predicted by a logistic regression fit on the other folds; samples whose prediction disagrees with their label are dropped, and most dropped samples are truly flipped (bar, pooled over all noisy runs). (3) Test accuracy of plain logistic regression, an untuned MLP and the filter (ours, purple) at 0, 20 and 40% noise; bars are means over 5 seeds (all runs, no selection), error bars are sd and dots are seeds. The filter stays closest to its clean-label accuracy as noise grows, and the MLP falls furthest.

figures.message: The filter's paired gain over both baselines is near zero or slightly negative on clean labels and grows with the noise rate, clearly so on digits.
figures.layout: Two small panels sharing the y axis: Digits (left), Breast cancer (right), named by small labels, no titles inside the plot. x: noise rate 0, 20, 40%. Two bars per x: filter minus logistic regression (muted blue, same hue as in Figure 1) and filter minus MLP (muted orange, same hue as in Figure 1); every bar is the filter's (ours) gain, and the legend names the baseline it is compared with. Bars are means over 5 seeds, error bars are 95% CIs of the paired difference, per-seed paired differences overlaid as dark dots. Gray zero line (reference). y: 'Accuracy gain of filter (points)', about -3 to 33. Legend above the panels, off the data.
figures.caption_draft: The filter's accuracy gain grows with label noise. Bars show the paired test-accuracy difference between the filter (ours) and each baseline, logistic regression and an untuned MLP, at each noise rate; bars are means over 5 seeds, error bars are 95% CIs and dots are individual seeds. Values below zero mean the baseline is better. On clean labels the gain is near zero against logistic regression and slightly negative against the MLP on digits; under noise every seed favors the filter over the MLP, and on digits the gain over logistic regression grows from 20 to 40% noise.
